summary: Snapshot is from a Jetson Orin Nano Super (cutie) running Ubuntu 22.04/L4T 36.5.2 acting as a robot compute node. ROS 2 Humble is installed but not sourced or running, so the live ROS graph is empty (0 nodes/topics) and no ROS-based device or actuator inventory could be captured. Physical peripherals visible via USB/serial enumeration include an STM32 STLink debug probe (ttyACM0), a Silicon Labs CP2102N UART bridge (ttyUSB0), a Seeed reSpeaker 4-mic USB audio array, a Realtek Bluetooth radio, and an unidentified QDtech MPI5001 HID device. Networking shows a wired Ethernet link as the default route, Wi-Fi and CAN interfaces administratively down, and two USB-gadget network links up. Docker is running; CUDA, colcon, rosdep, vcstool are installed. Memory usage is moderate (58%) but swap usage is comparatively high (43.7%). No actuator inventory or ROS device inventory entries exist, consistent with the ROS stack being installed but never launched in this snapshot rather than evidence of missing hardware.
highest_priority_next_check: Confirm with the operator whether ROS 2 nodes are expected to be running at this time before treating this as a fault.
successful_checks: CPU snapshot is below the warning threshold (0.0%).
Memory snapshot is below the warning threshold (58.2%).
No collected filesystem is at or above 90% usage.
All collected thermal readings are below their reported critical limits.
Default network route is present on enP8p1s0.
architecture_observations: Single Jetson Orin Nano Super module serves as the onboard compute/robot controller (board_name Jetson, L4T 36.5.2, MAXN_SUPER power mode).

ROS 2 Humble is installed (197 indexed packages) but the environment is not sourced and no ROS 2 processes are running, so ros_runtime_inventory reports an UNAVAILABLE graph with 0 nodes/topics/services/actions — this reflects an inactive runtime, not necessarily an application fault.

robot_state_publisher, colcon, rosdep, vcstool, and CUDA toolkit are installed, suggesting a colcon/ROS2-based robotics workspace is intended to run on this host, but no build/runtime artifacts are exposed in this snapshot.

Peripheral hardware is exposed purely through Linux device/USB enumeration (serial_devices, usb_devices, sensor_inventory) rather than through ROS topics/nodes, since no ROS graph is active — so ownership of these devices by any particular ROS node cannot be established from this snapshot alone.

Two independent USB controllers are populated: a USB2 hub tree (bus 1) carrying the STLink probe, CP210x bridge, Bluetooth radio, reSpeaker mic array, and QDtech MPI5001 HID device; and an empty USB3 hub tree (bus 2) with no attached peripheral devices reported.

Networking is anchored on wired Ethernet (enP8p1s0, 1000 Mbps full duplex, default route, internet reachable) while Wi-Fi (wlP1p1s0) and CAN (can0) interfaces exist but are administratively down; two USB-gadget interfaces (usb0/usb1) are up without IPv4 addresses, and docker0 is present due to the running Docker service.
Memory is at 58.2% used with swap 43.7% used — a moderate combined memory pressure signal worth watching but not yet a confirmed fault given no process-level breakdown is available.
unknowns: Whether ttyUSB0 (CP2102N UART bridge) is required by an active robot service, or is an idle/optional peripheral — permission denial alone does not establish operational necessity.
The functional role of the QDtech MPI5001 USB HID device (e.g., touchscreen, controller, or diagnostic panel) — no descriptive metadata beyond USB IDs is present.

Whether can0 being down is expected (CAN bus unused in this configuration) or represents a disconnected/misconfigured actuator communication link — no expected_state evidence ties CAN to a required subsystem.
Whether wlP1p1s0 (Wi-Fi) being down is an intentional design choice (wired-primary network) or an unintended regression, since no expected_state data confirms Wi-Fi is required.
Purpose of usb0/usb1 USB-gadget network interfaces being up without addresses — could be an unused peripheral tethering path or an incompletely configured link.
Root cause of elevated swap usage (43.7%) — no per-process memory data is available to determine whether this is due to a leaking process, expected buffering, or historical peak usage.
Whether the reSpeaker mic array (marked PRESENT_NOT_EXERCISED) is meant to be actively used by any ROS audio pipeline, since no ROS audio node/topic evidence exists in the (currently empty) graph.

issues.title: Current user lacks read-write access to /dev/ttyUSB0.
issues.expected_state: Only serial interfaces required by the robot profile or runtime need stable, read-write access.
issues.operational_impact: No operational impact is proven until the operator confirms this component is required.
probable_causes: Serial identity, driver binding, permissions, or port ownership inconsistency.
primary_approach: Confirm that this serial interface is required before changing permissions or identity rules.
success_criteria: The intended process can identify and access the stable serial device without contention.

issues.title: ROS 2 Humble installed but shell environment not sourced
issues.expected_state: If ROS 2-based robot software is expected to run on this host, the shell/service environment should have ROS_DISTRO, AMENT/COLCON overlays, and RMW configuration sourced so ros2 CLI and node discovery function.
issues.operational_impact: No live ROS graph can be inspected or is running; any robot application depending on ROS 2 topics/services/actions is currently not operating from this snapshot's perspective.
observed: ROS installation detected=true, environment_sourced=false, active_distribution=null, running=false, state=INSTALLED
probable_causes: Systemd services or launch scripts not configured to source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash before executing ROS 2 processes.
ROS 2 stack intentionally not started at time of snapshot capture.
primary_approach: Confirm with the operator whether ROS 2 nodes are expected to be running at this time before treating this as a fault.
If expected to run, verify service/unit files or startup scripts source the ROS 2 environment prior to node execution.
alternative_approaches: Check systemd service definitions for ExecStart lines lacking environment sourcing.
Review container/Docker entrypoints since Docker is running — ROS nodes may be intended to run inside containers with their own sourcing.
success_criteria: ROS 2 environment variables (ROS_DISTRO, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION) are set in the intended execution context.
ros2 node/topic list return expected entries once environment and processes are active (subject to operator confirmation of intended state).

issues.title: Live ROS 2 graph inspection unavailable / empty graph
issues.expected_state: If a robot application is intended to be active, the ROS 2 graph should show non-zero nodes/topics matching the deployed robot stack.
issues.operational_impact: No ROS-level visibility into nodes, topics, services, or actions; downstream diagnosis of any ROS-based subsystem (motion, sensors, control) cannot proceed until the graph is queryable.
observed: state=UNAVAILABLE, nodes=0, topics=0, services=0, actions=0, discovery_mode=unavailable, environment_recovered=false
probable_causes: Downstream effect of ROS environment not being sourced (see ROS_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_SOURCED).
No ROS 2 processes launched at time of snapshot.
primary_approach: Confirm with the operator whether any ROS 2 nodes should be active at snapshot time.
If yes, request ros_node_info / ros_topic_info probes after confirming environment is sourced in the target shell/service context.
alternative_approaches: Inspect systemd/container service status for any ROS-launching units before assuming absence of graph reflects a fault.
success_criteria: ros_node_info and ros_topic_info return a non-empty, expected node/topic set consistent with the intended robot software configuration.

issues.title: Swap usage elevated at 43.7% while physical memory usage is 58.2%
issues.expected_state: Under normal operation with 3.3GB of available physical memory remaining, swap usage would typically remain low unless memory pressure events have occurred.
issues.operational_impact: Potential indicator of past or recurring memory pressure; could contribute to latency in memory-intensive robotics/vision workloads if swapping occurs during active operation, though no confirmed performance impact is evidenced here.
observed: memory usage_percent=58.2, swap_usage_percent=43.7, swap_used_bytes=1743257600 of swap_total_bytes=3988414464
probable_causes: A memory-intensive process consumed swap earlier in the current uptime (44183s ~12.3h) and has not released it.
zram-backed swap devices (zram0-5) are in active use as part of normal Jetson memory management tuning.
primary_approach: Treat as advisory; monitor for correlation with performance degradation before further action.
Confirm with operator whether this swap level is typical baseline for this deployment or a recent change.
alternative_approaches: Review process-level memory consumption history if available through other tooling (not covered by allowed probes here).
success_criteria: No OOM-kill or memory-pressure kernel log entries correlate with current uptime, or operator confirms this swap level is expected baseline.
